testCoverage.summary: This README documentation file has no automated tests or validation. The primary concerns are: (1) malformed command formatting where commands are concatenated with descriptions without proper separation, creating a high risk of copy-paste errors; (2) no validation that the documented command sequence actually works; (3) platform-specific path examples without cross-platform considerations. Priority should be given to creating an integration test that validates the command sequence works as documented, followed by implementing markdown/documentation linting to catch formatting issues.

refactorings.summary: The README file needs significant formatting improvements. The main issues are: (1) commands and descriptions run together without separation, making them hard to read, (2) no markdown formatting despite being a GitHub README, (3) inconsistent presentation of commands versus output, and (4) missing structural elements like headers and sections. Converting to README.md with proper markdown syntax, code blocks, and clear separation between commands and descriptions would transform this into a professional, readable tutorial.

recommendations.description: Commands and their descriptions are concatenated without proper separation (lines 2-4), making the README difficult to read and prone to copy-paste errors. Separate commands from descriptions using line breaks and consider converting to README.md with proper markdown code blocks.

The command sequence in the README has no automated validation to ensure it actually works as documented. Implement an integration test that executes the documented steps in a clean environment to verify accuracy.

Convert the plain text README to README.md with proper markdown formatting (headers, code blocks, sections) to improve readability and leverage GitHub's rendering capabilities. This will provide clear visual hierarchy and make commands easily copyable.

The README contains macOS-specific paths (e.g., '/Users/your_user_directory/') without noting platform differences. Use generic path placeholders or add platform-specific notes to support Linux and Windows users.

The README lacks standard sections such as project description, prerequisites (e.g., Git installation requirement), and structured setup instructions. Add these sections to follow documentation best practices.
